subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw ship a public memory-search exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should that contract cover builtin indexing only or builtin plus QMD/status/index-identity behavior together?
rationale: The request changes public memorySearch configuration and indexed recall semantics; repository policy treats config/default additions and memory/session state as compatibility-sensitive rather than a narrow automatic bug fix.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor after matcher repair, index identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs, while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Hold the exclusion config until builtin, QMD, watcher behavior, stale-index cleanup, docs, and diagnostics share one accepted exclusion model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and focus on clearer path-drift, broad-extraPaths, and benchmark-contamination guidance plus status warnings.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor after matcher repair, index identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs, while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and extended the existing QMD extraPaths contract, making them the best routing candidate for backend scope and config semantics.
